title: Pompeii — the city that died in a day
style: documentary photograph, Roman Campania, hard Mediterranean light, ash grey and terracotta, fine grain, no text, no watermark, no modern objects
negative: no modern buildings, no tourists, no signage, no cartoon, no illustration

lines.vo: Pompeii was not frozen in time, the volcano buried it.
lines.title: NOT FROZEN
lines.image: the excavated streets of Pompeii with the cone of Vesuvius on the skyline behind, hard daylight, no people

lines.vo: The town sat six miles from Vesuvius, downwind.
Pumice and ash fell on the roofs for hours.
People went out to the road, trying to reach the sea.
Then the pyroclastic flows came down the flank onto the town.
caption: Not falling.
FLOWING.

lines.vo: The ash sealed each body where it lay.
caption: Sealed
where it lay.

lines.vo: The body inside decayed away to nothing.
What was left was a cavity in the ash, shaped like a person.
caption: A hollow
where a person
had been.

lines.vo: Diggers poured plaster into the cavity and let it set.
The plaster came out as the shape of the person.
Pompeii did not preserve the people, it preserved the space they left behind.
lines.title: THE SPACE
